rotating_electrode.title: Rotating Electrode Residual Chlorine Measurement
rotating_electrode.subtitle: The patented rotating-electrode structure helps reduce surface fouling and supports stable long-duration residual chlorine monitoring.
rotating_electrode.description: Waterbee's rotating-electrode approach continuously conditions the electrode surface to reduce membrane-consumable burden and to suppress error caused by fouling or changing field flow. It is designed with both maintainability and measurement confidence in mind for continuous operation at water treatment sites.

points.title: Low-maintenance membrane-light structure
points.description: The design reduces the consumable-replacement burden typically associated with membrane-based methods.

points.title: Stable under flow and fouling changes
points.description: The rotating electrode and coated surface help minimize error caused by flow variation and contamination buildup.

points.title: Built for continuous duty
points.description: Ongoing surface conditioning helps suppress signal drift during extended operation.

strengths: Continuous rotation helps mitigate fouling buildup on the electrode surface.
Reduced consumable burden can lower maintenance cost and replacement frequency.
The structure suits continuous-duty environments such as waterworks and clearwells.
considerations: Regular checks on sample condition and electrode status are still important for optimal performance.
Sites with large pH or sample-composition variation may require operating-condition review.
Measurement confidence improves when the sampling path and flow cell are kept clean.

scattering.title: 90° Scattered-Light Turbidity Measurement
scattering.subtitle: A low-range optical layout that clearly positions the light source, sample cell, and 90° detector for readable turbidity change.
scattering.description: Waterbee's turbidity approach separates the illumination axis from the detector axis so that scattered light can be read more consistently. The structure is intended for sites where low turbidity matters, such as clearwells and water treatment facilities.

points.title: Visible optical layout
points.description: The light source location and sample path are intentionally easy to understand for maintenance and operation.

points.title: Dedicated scattered-light readout
points.description: The detector reads the 90° scattered signal rather than the transmitted beam, improving sensitivity to low turbidity change.

points.title: Interference awareness
points.description: The structure is arranged with attention to microbubbles, cell condition, and optical contamination.

strengths: The optical structure is suitable for reading subtle turbidity changes in low-range operation.
The source–cell–detector relationship is easy to interpret during maintenance work.
It provides an intuitive way to explain continuous turbidity monitoring behavior.
considerations: Flow-cell cleanliness and optical surface condition directly influence measurement confidence.
Microbubbles and sample flow characteristics should be considered when reading turbidity trends.
Low-range turbidity operation depends heavily on stable sampling and piping conditions.

controller.title: ESP32-Based Smart Controller
controller.subtitle: A next-generation control platform is being prepared to combine sensor acquisition, local control, and Wi-Fi · Bluetooth connectivity in one device.
controller.description: The new controller concept is being designed around an ESP32-based architecture that supports sensor data acquisition and local control while strengthening Wi-Fi and Bluetooth connectivity alongside existing wired outputs. The goal is an operational controller that also improves site commissioning, local inspection, and mobile access.

points.title: One platform for sensing and control
points.description: It is intended to collect inputs from residual chlorine, turbidity, pH/EC, and other sensors while handling local control outputs.

points.title: Improved site setup convenience
points.description: Bluetooth-based short-range access is planned to improve laptop or mobile accessibility during installation and inspection.

points.title: Preserved higher-level integration
points.description: Even with wireless connectivity, compatibility with RS-485, 4~20mA, and relay-based field integration remains important.

strengths: The concept supports both wireless setup convenience and existing wired plant integration.
It can expand both local HMI behavior and mobile accessibility in the field.
The platform is flexible for future sensor expansion and firmware feature growth.
considerations: Wireless quality will still depend on installation location and RF conditions at the site.
Firmware update and access-control strategy should be planned together with the hardware.
Critical facilities should still pair wireless features with stable power and wired fallback paths.
